en: Regarding the Dharma-Assembly Altar for the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara of Kāyagiri:
if there are śramaṇas, brāhmaṇas, or any sons and daughters of good family who wish—
One who upholds the Dharma of a bodhisattva should construct a mandala measuring four cubits.
One should seek out an excellent site, a pure location, and sweep and sprinkle it until it is clean.
The ground was smeared with scented water and cow dung;
various multicolored banners, canopies, precious bells, pendants, and mirrors were suspended [therefrom],
and the site of practice (maṇḍala) was adorned with gold and silver interspersed in every variety.
In the center of the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa), he established a five-colored altar measuring four cubits in length and breadth.
First white was laid down, followed by yellow, then red, and finally black.
Construct four gates;
in the center of the altar,
fashion a lotus seat and install an image of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.
At the eastern gate, construct a magnificent throne and install an Eleven-faced Bodhisattva.
At the northern gate, construct a lotus throne and install an Eight-armed Avalokiteśvara.
In the south, install the eight dragon kings.
The Nanda Dragon King,
the Vāsuki Dragon King,
and the Takṣaka Dragon King.
The Naga King Karkoṭaka,
the Naga King Padma,
and the Naga King Mahāpadma.
The Naga King Śaṅkhapāla and the Naga King Kūlika—
these eight nāgas offered only non-glutinous rice with milk gruel;
the others made various offerings and were likewise able to light forty-five lamps.
First, summon the eight Dragon Kings; they come and go using the *Yakṣe Yakṣe* body-seal.
Recite: *Oṃ yakṣe yakṣe 2 āṭaṅkāra yakṣe 3 ālaṃtū 4 svāhā 5*. This [mantra] is near the western gate of the maṇḍala.
In the southern capital, one prepares a hearth and mixes sesame seeds, rice grains, and flowers with ghee and honey.
Reciting the heart mantra while casting them into the fire, one performs this one thousand and eight times. Thereafter, one invokes the Bodhisattva Acalaketu (Acala).
Next, perform the approach and departure for the eight-armed Avalokiteśvara body-seal:
Oṃ niye śaye jhaḍaṃ svāhā. Then, perform the approach and departure for the flower-seat seal.
Having thus invited the Eleven-faced Bodhisattva, [proceed as follows].
One should scatter various kinds of flowers and burn all manner of famous incenses,
such as aloeswood, frankincense, and sandalwood, to make offerings.
The mantra-practitioner shall not eat for one day.
If one cannot endure hunger, one may consume only ghee.
Having bathed with fragrant water and donned new, clean garments,
one shall enter the maṇḍala and perform offerings.
One shall always be mindful of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva;
furthermore, one should also master the methods of the Krodha Vajra for establishing boundaries and making offerings.
One should protect the body and establish the boundary using mantras and mudrās.
Recite the mantra over a wooden staff seven times, or over water seven times;
furthermore, seal the water with the mudrā and mantra,
or recite it over white mustard seeds, ashes, and so forth, seven times.
Plant wooden stakes at the four corners to establish the boundary.
Scatter mustard seeds, ashes, and water in the ten directions to complete the consecration of the boundary (*sīmābandha*).
With the two hands bound externally, extend the two index fingers straight upward, keeping them about five *aṅgula* apart.
Place the two thumbs together;
bend each one at a single joint, ensuring they do not touch the index fingers.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ pravicāsta vajra śarvara rucaye svāhā. To perform the *khadga-mudrā* (sword seal), extend both hands with the left hand outside and the right hand inside.
Place the left palm upon the back of the right hand and extend the thumbs of both hands.
*Oṃ āsamayini svāhā*. For the Great Dharmakāya Seal: perform the outer binding with both hands and join the two little fingers upright together.
With both thumbs held upright and touching, bend them and move the thumbs back and forth.

Oṃ (1) duna duna (2) matha matha (3) khāda khāda (4) hāyagarbha (5) hūṃ phaṭ (6) svāhā (7). Next, for the Heart Seal of Hāyagarbha: perform the outer binding with both hands, with the two thumbs held upright and touching.
Bend each finger at one joint so that they do not touch the index fingers;
move the thumbs back and forth.
*Oṃ amṛtodbhave hūṃ phaṭ svāhā*. Next, for the head mudrā: form the outer-bound hand gesture (*bāhyabandha*) and extend both index fingers.
The heads [of the hands] are pressed together, with the joints of the two thumbs each bent;
the tips of the little fingers also [touch].

*Tadyathā*: (1) *Cakrāvebhaya*, (2) *Cakragacchāvebhaya*, (3) *Cakrapadma-kṣari-bhaya*, (4) *Amuka* (pronounced with a departing tone)—here one calls out the person's name—(5) *Śirakīra* (the first syllable pronounced high, the second a conjunct), (6) *Prasamgaccha* (the first syllable pronounced high), (7) *Tu*, (8) *Svāhā*. (The departing tone applies to all subsequent instances. Next, the *Mūrdhan-mudrā* (Crown Seal) follows the previous *Śiras-mudrā* (Head Seal).
Simply change the position so that the tips of the two index fingers touch each other, and arrange the two middle fingers in front of the two index fingers with their tips touching.
*Oṃ śrīlīji hūṃ phaṭ svāhā*. For the mouth seal (*mukhamudrā*): interlace the little fingers and ring fingers of both hands within, and touch the tips of the two middle fingers together.
Extend both thumbs upright;
with the right forefinger, pinch the tip of the right thumb.
The left index finger is extended slightly curved, positioned beside the middle finger.
Oṃ hulu lu krodhana huṃ phaṭ svāhā. Next, the fang mudrā is the same as the fang mudrā of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva Amoghapāśa mentioned previously.
Above, following the modification, the two middle fingers are held straight and upright with their tips touching.
The two thumbs are held side-by-side and upright, pressed against the middle fingers.
First, the left little finger grasps the back of the right ring finger.
Grasp the back of the left ring finger with the right ring finger.

*Namaḥ āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya mahākāruṇikāya tadyathā trāṭ trāṭ mātā mātā cinda cinda binda binda hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā.* This is the Great Dharani of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.

Furthermore, as for the *Avalokiteśvara-viśeṣa-mahā-mantra* and this other mantra, the *Bhaṭṭāraka-siddha-paṭṭi*—translated into Chinese as "Accomplishment through Recitation"—even if one does not maintain the ritual or perform offerings at the altar, accomplishment is achieved simply by reciting it.
If one wishes to dispatch Hayagrīva Avalokiteśvara,
one should hold a *sūlabhūṣpa* (or, according to another tradition, a *pātra* flower) and recite the mantra once.
Strike the image once;
repeat this seven times, then depart. The mantra is as follows:
Tadyathā: sarapara-sarā, jaya-vijayā, vajra-kūṭa-sambhava, svāpana-kacchamudrikā, svāhā.
